questions.q: When checking the finished package against Lesson 46's scope, what determines whether the project is actually complete?
options: Whether the video narration has been recorded
Every stage (Extract, Transform, Load, Log) does what was originally scoped — not whether it has extra features
Whether the package has more transformations than any other student's package
Whether the package can extract from every table in AdventureWorks2012 at once
questions.explain: Completeness here means matching the original scope row by row — the same discipline this catalog's other capstone-wrap-up lessons use, not adding unscoped features.

questions.q: When presenting the package, what should come first — the problem statement or the implementation details?
options: A list of every SSIS keyboard shortcut used while building it
A one-sentence statement of the problem, before walking through control flow and data flow
The exact runtime in milliseconds of the most recent execution
The Derived Column expression syntax, in full detail
questions.explain: Leading with a plain-language problem statement, then control flow, then data flow, then the incremental/error-handling additions, is the order that actually communicates what the project demonstrates.

questions.q: Why does the guide say to be ready to explain WHY the Lookup runs before the OLE DB Destination, specifically?
options: Because the Lookup transformation is optional and could be removed
Because that ordering decision is a fair proxy for whether you understand dimensional loading, not just SSIS's UI
Because interviewers only ever ask about component ordering
Because SSIS randomizes component order at runtime
questions.explain: Explaining that ordering decision shows real understanding of why a surrogate key has to be resolved before a fact row can be written — not just familiarity with dragging components onto a canvas.

questions.q: Which two courses does this lesson point to as logical next steps in the catalog?
options: Blockchain Development and Salesforce Administration
Excel and PowerShell
There are no further courses recommended
SSRS Development and Data Modeling & Data Warehousing
questions.explain: SSRS Development builds reports on top of exactly this kind of warehouse-style data, and Data Modeling & Data Warehousing goes deeper into the star-schema design decisions this capstone only touched.

questions.q: What should a portfolio-ready description of this project include, according to the lesson?
options: Only a screenshot of the SSIS Toolbox
A video of the package running with no other documentation
Nothing — SSIS packages can't be shown to anyone outside the company that built them
A kept .dtsx package file and a short README describing the databases and architecture — an inspectable artifact, not just a resume line
questions.explain: A resume sentence alone can't be verified; keeping the actual package file plus a README describing the two databases and the architecture table turns this into something a reviewer can actually inspect.
